# Context before the first observation

This is an informed desired-source study for Issue #44 and the generic boundary
of #27/#43, authored after reading the live Issues, current Reference, shared
AST/type/resolution code, sized generic checking and specialization. No external
model is invoked; the exact deployed model/sampling settings are not recorded.
It is not a zero-prior benchmark, a new Guardian interpretation or a proof.

The eight abstract programs are desired forms. The current parser has no Basis
parameter kind. The separate concrete Bit control uses existing Nat/Op syntax.
Save every source and schema-2 edition-2026 manifest before invoking the CLI.
Expected later owner/capability/type failures must not be claimed from an earlier
parser rejection. Repeat uses only k <= 4, with no maximum-size request.

The proposed experiment keeps an abstract A opaque: move it, return it and apply
an explicitly constrained Op<A>. It grants no width reflection, decomposition,
preparation or automatic coherence. Later instances must preserve Bit/Bits<1>,
Unit/Bits<0>, complete tuple trees, phase, ordered axes and linear ownership.
Host type bindings and concrete source type-literal grammar remain implementation
choices to settle in the Issue before behavior changes; these original sources
will not be rewritten to fit those choices.

The baseline is published faa5cfb5e7ea1cf3b39a43b80f7f2345e89197c2, plus the
ongoing test/doc-only discovery repair. Record exact original source/CLI/native
identities and actual diagnostics. Reuse the existing built/audited kernel; this
observation is not a fresh local Lean build, admission or release validation.
